alerts.title: Weight Gain on TLD
alerts.message: Guidelines state the possibility of weight gain should be discussed when starting all ART regimens. Patient has gained weight since starting TLD, with a current BMI of 32.4 kg/m² and acanthosis nigricans noted. Weight gain could be attributed to TLD, but non-drug causes such as diet and exercise should also be considered.

Complaints & Symptoms:
36-year-old woman presents for routine review. Mentions her clothes no longer fit and she has gained 'a lot of weight' since starting her current HIV medication. Also feels more tired than usual.

Examination Findings:
BP 138/88 mmHg. Weight 82kg. BMI 32.4 kg/m². Waist circumference 96cm. Acanthosis nigricans noted at neck and axillae. No peripheral oedema.

Significant history prior to today's visit:
ART History: Switched from TDF/3TC/EFV (used for 3 years) to TLD 18 months ago due to EFV-related side effects (dizziness and vivid dreams).

Baseline Metrics (at TLD switch): BP was 118/74 mmHg; Weight was 65kg; BMI was 25.6 kg/m²; Fasting glucose was 92 mg/dL.

Comorbidities/Family History: HIV diagnosed 2019. No prior DM or HTN. Family history significant for Type 2 Diabetes (mother).

Consolidated Guidelines for the Prevention and Treatment of HIV and Aids in Uganda - 2022 **Drug substitutions for ARV drug toxicity** Substitution is the process of replacing one ARV drug with another. The duration on ART is important when doing ARV substitution. If substitutions are being done within six months of starting ART, it is not necessary to perform a viral load test. However, after six months on ART, a viral load test may be required to rule out treatment failure before a drug is substituted in a failing patient. If the viral load is not suppressed, it is possible the patient may be failing on treatment. Follow the viral load algorithm to rule out treatment failure. In a failing patient, the ART regimen should be switched to 2nd line.
